correctness.rationale: Fock monomials diagonalize the annular Toeplitz contraction with eigenvalues Gamma(k+1,1) interval probabilities. Exact integration by parts gives a single-sign-change adjacent recurrence, hence consecutive maximizing blocks; mode degree is the logarithmic mean of the interval endpoints up to one. Uniform exponential-sum Berry–Esseen gives the Gaussian window with \(O(R^{-1/2})\) error per degree on all \(O(\sqrt R)\)-long optimizing blocks. Uniform Riemann sums yield \(O(1)\) absolute error in the sharp Ky Fan partial sum. Concavity of sorted partial sums gives the ordered spectral derivative. Fubini verifies the normal convolution formula and strict gap. All bounds treat every fixed a<b,c>0 and large real R; finite diagnostics are not used in place of the proof.

originality.rationale: Exact gamma eigenvalues and the Ky Fan variational principle are established prior facts. The claim instead derives a sharp two-edge critical-width ordered spectral limit, all finite-rank consecutive monomial optimizers, and an \(O(1)\) absolute error for the sharp growing-rank total concentration in a regime excluded by fixed-ratio plunge estimates and van-Hove filling laws. Published mathematical searches and the accessible own claim record contained no implication covering this package. The unresolved risk is independently published Gaussian boundary-crossover statements under other terminology.

value.rationale: This is the critical transition where two Gaussian spectral edges overlap because annular physical thickness stays constant. The theorem solves both full ordered spectral classification and the exact leading best capture for a growing orthonormal family, with bounded absolute error and a strict quantitative deficit below rank and geometric-trace limits. It is a natural boundary-dominated localization problem outside the established fixed-ratio plunge and van-Hove state-counting regimes, not a made-up slice of a numerical table.
